scope: Current platform-behavior assertions and common misuse risks only. Creative frameworks remain source heuristics. This artifact does not edit source concepts.

primary_sources.title: Understand your content performance for YouTube's recommendation system
Understand external factors for YouTube's recommendation system
Measure key moments for audience retention

checks.boundary: YouTube explicitly says its system finds videos for viewers and personalizes recommendations; 'prediction engine' is source metaphor, not a complete architecture.
Viewing/search history and current video vary by surface; exact age/device/time signals asserted by speaker are not established by these pages.
Official current Help page does not document the lecture's exact two-network production implementation. Historical research is not proof of present internals.
Satisfaction matters, but official guidance separately names appeal and engagement, plus multiple recommendation signals; 'only' overstates.
Official sources do not establish that a cross-video session contribution guarantees more recommendations for a creator video.
Engagement and satisfaction matter; retention and return rate are not the sole currency or a fixed formula.
Native A/B test can compare up to three title/thumbnail options under defined eligibility; serial manual edits and video-batch comparisons are different experiments.
No official fixed 3–5 video or 48–72 hour diagnostic threshold. Low impressions may reflect demand, competition, eligibility, and audience response.
Funnel is useful for investigating possible causes, but no row proves a sole cause; CTR and watch behavior require traffic-source and audience context.
70–80/20–30 allocation is supplied creator advice; no official platform threshold is asserted.
Engagement and audience-retention analysis are official concepts; 60–90-second progression and 7–10 turns are not official rules.
Seven-item 35-point scorecard and its bands are source-defined; no platform endorsement or predictive calibration.
Official source names appeal, engagement, satisfaction. The specific topic/title/thumbnail and hook/story/pacing mapping is a project interpretation of these buckets.
CTR and audience-retention reports are YouTube Studio Analytics for a creator's own video; public competitor pages do not expose the competitor's private graphs.
Topic interest and competition matter; a transferred format alone does not prove demand or guarantee reach.
Sequential topic or audience-desire testing is not native concurrent YouTube title/thumbnail A/B testing.
